body.en: A continuous random variable X has a probability density function (p.d.f.) $f(x)$ with $f(x) \ge 0$ and $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = 1$. Probabilities are areas: $P(a < X < b) = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$. For any single value, $P(X = a) = 0$, so $<$ and $\le$ give the same probability. The distribution function is $F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{x} f(t)\,dt$, and $E(X) = \int x f(x)\,dx$.

points.en: P(a < X < b) = area from a to b

narration.en: A probability density function is never negative and has total area one. The probability of an interval is the area under the curve over that interval.

body.en: For a continuous variable the height f(x) is not a probability: it can even exceed 1. Only areas under the curve are probabilities.
